title: Developer Experience Docs: SDK Guides, Quickstarts, API Examples, Ops & Top Support Issues (Playbook)
author: Sofia Patel
body:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook consolidates guidance, templates, and canonical fixes for the Developer Experience (DevEx) documentation surface: SDK guides, quickstarts & templates, API examples, docs-site operating procedures, and the top support issues that repeatedly surface in support channels. The goal is to make documentation consistent, discoverable, and low-friction for both external developers and internal support/solutions teams.

Scope: eng-developer-experience quickstarts-and-templates; cross-references to docs-site and SDK repos.

Owner & Contacts
- Doc owner: eng-devexp-docs (primary contact: sofia.patel@redwood.ai)
- Backing teams: SDK engineers, API platform, Developer Relations
- On-call doc support: devex-oncall rotation (see /confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts for rotation calendar)

Summary of Principles
- Keep examples copy-pasteable: all code snippets must run locally with only minimal env setup.
- Single source of truth: prefer canonical examples in SDK repo (github.com/redwood-inference/devx-sdks) and mirror in docs site via include mechanism.
- Fast feedback loop: triage doc-related issues in weekly doc triage; critical/regression issues escalate to SDK owners within 24 hours.
- Observability: instrument top doc pages with search click-through and time-on-page metrics; target 99% uptime for docs static site.

Structure of this Playbook
1) SDK Guides: standards and template
2) Quickstarts & Templates: file naming, minimal examples, and onboarding flow
3) API Examples: canonical patterns and supported features (streaming, function calls, embeddings)
4) Docs Site Ops: SLA, release process, and migration checklist
5) Top Support Issues & Canonical Fixes: recurring problems and step-by-step resolutions
6) Appendix: sample code snippets, config tables, and templates

1) SDK Guides: standards and template
- Purpose: explain idiomatic usage for each supported language (Python, TypeScript/Node, Go, Java).
- Required sections for each SDK guide page (must appear in order):
  1. Short intro (1-2 paragraphs).
  2. Installation & quick verify command.
  3. Authentication (examples for API key + environment variable + KMS integration note).
  4. Core primitives (client, request/response model).
  5. Streaming examples (where supported).
  6. Error handling & retries (with status codes and retry policy).
  7. Advanced patterns (batching, caching, function-calling).
  8. Troubleshooting & common errors (link to support playbook).
  9. API reference link + changelog notes.
- Template filename pattern: sdk-<lang>-guide-YYYY-MM-DD.json (e.g., sdk-python-guide-2026-03-15.json).
- Minimal content requirement: each SDK guide must include a runnable quickstart that performs at least one generation and one embedding call using the public sandbox model.

Python SDK quick verify (example to include in page):
- Prereq: pip install redwood-sdk>=0.9.0
- Verify snippet (must be runnable):
  ```python
  from redwood import RedwoodClient
  client = RedwoodClient(api_key="$REDWOOD_API_KEY")
  resp = client.text.generate(model="open-redwood/sandbox-1", prompt="Hello from docs!")
  print(resp.text)
  ```

2) Quickstarts & Templates
- Quickstarts are 1-2 page guides that get a developer from zero to a working integration in under 15 minutes.
- Each quickstart must include: objective, pre-reqs, step-by-step instructions, verification step, and next steps.
- Template categories: chat, text generation, embeddings search, reranking, streaming responses, and function/tool calling.
- Naming convention: quickstart-<topic>-<lang>-YYYY-MM-DD.json (e.g., quickstart-embeddings-python-2026-06-10.json).
- Boilerplate checklist (must be present in each quickstart):
  - Objective (one sentence)
  - Estimated time to complete (minutes)
  - Cost estimate (token usage range or sandbox note)
  - Required permissions & roles (e.g., API key with embeddings:read)
  - Verification tests (exact commands/assertions)

3) API Examples (canonical patterns)
- Purpose: demonstrate best-practice API usage for common workflows. Keep examples small (25-80 lines).
- Canonical APIs to cover: text generation, chat messages, streaming generation, embeddings, batch embeddings, function calling, and model rollouts.
- Example: curling the hosted API for streaming generation:
  curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"open-redwood/sandbox-1","input":"Write a haiku about latency"}' \
    https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate/stream
- Error matrix to document for each endpoint (status code -> cause -> resolution). Minimal required entries:
  - 400: malformed request -> validate JSON schema; include example of corrective payload.
  - 401: invalid/expired API key -> rotate key and update env var.
  - 429: rate limit -> surface Retry-After and recommend exponential backoff with jitter.
  - 503: capacity degraded -> failover to compatible model variant (document model mapping table).

4) Docs Site Operations (operating procedures)
- SLOs & targets:
  - Docs static site availability: 99.9% monthly.
  - Example pages load time (p95): < 600ms.
  - Search freshness: updated index within 5 minutes of a merged docs change.
- Release process for docs content:
  1. Author edits in markdown and opens PR in docs repo (docs-site).
  2. Automated lint & link-check runs on PR (CI job: docs-ci).
  3. Reviewer from DevEx assigned; approvals required: 1 tech + 1 writer for changes that affect external behavior.
  4. Merge & staged deploy to docs-staging.redwood.ai.
  5. Smoke tests (see below) run; if green, promote to production during a daily deploy window (02:00-03:00 UTC).
- Smoke tests (automated):
  - Verify home page returns 200 and contains expected headline.
  - Verify 20 canonical quickstarts return 200 and load within 1200ms.
  - Run link-checker; fail on 4xx links.
- Rollback criteria: any smoke test failure or customer-facing regression reported by >1 customer within 2 hours should trigger rollback.

5) Top Support Issues & Canonical Fixes (current list)
- Issue: "SDK: Invalid API Key errors when using environment variable in Docker"
  Canonical fix:
  1. Confirm API key present in image at runtime: run `docker run --env REDWOOD_API_KEY ... env` and verify.
  2. Document best practice: bind API key through runtime secrets (K8s secret or cloud secret manager) rather than bake into image.
  3. Add verification snippet to quickstarts (e.g., `print(os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))`).
  Ownership: SDK team.

- Issue: "Large embedding batch requests time out or exceed memory"
  Canonical fix:
  1. Recommend batching strategy: prefer batches <= 1024 vectors or 1M total tokens per request.
  2. Provide sample code that streams embeddings and writes partial results to persistent storage.
  3. Suggest using the batch embeddings API (POST /v1/embeddings/batch) with `max_batch_size` param.
  Ownership: API Platform + Applied ML.

- Issue: "Streaming responses stop mid-message when using serverless proxies"
  Canonical fix:
  1. Confirm proxy supports chunked transfer encoding; add note to serverless quickstarts.
  2. Suggest using a long-lived connection endpoint (dedicated route) or upgrading proxy timeout to >300s.
  Ownership: Eng Platform + DevRel.

- Issue: "Function calling returns ambiguous argument types (numbers vs strings)"
  Canonical fix:
  1. Update function schema examples to strongly type params and include JSON schema validation on client side.
  2. Add explicit example: `{"type":"object","properties":{"amount":{"type":"number"}}}` and corresponding SDK validation snippet.
  Ownership: Applied ML + SDK.

- Issue: "Docs quickstart examples fail due to model deprecation"
  Canonical fix:
  1. Maintain a model-mapping table in repo (models.yaml) that maps deprecated -> current model.
  2. CI job: docs-model-mapper runs nightly to detect references to deprecated models and opens PRs to replace them.
  Ownership: Model Onboarding + DevEx.

6) Templates & Examples (appendix)
- Quickstart template header (copyable):
  ---
  title: "Quickstart: <topic> (<lang>)"
  objective: "<one-sentence objective>"
  estimated_time_minutes: "15"
  cost_estimate: "sandbox/no-cost / ~50-200 tokens"
  pre_reqs: ["API key", "python 3.10+"]
  ---
- Minimal troubleshooting table (to include on each page):
  | Symptom | Likely cause | Quick fix | Owner |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 401 on first request | Missing/invalid API key | Ensure env var set; rotate key | SDK |
  | 429 when sending bursts | Exceeded rate limit | Backoff + request jitter; check quotas | API Platform |
  | Streaming cuts off | Proxy timeout or chunked transfer not supported | Use compatible proxy or increase timeout | Eng Platform |

- Sample model mapping snippet (models.yaml example text to include in repo):
  models:
    sandbox-1: open-redwood/sandbox-1
    text-1: open-redwood/text-1

Maintenance & Review Cadence
- Quarterly: content accuracy review for all quickstarts and SDK guides. Responsible: doc owner + SDK lead.
- Monthly: surface top 10 search queries and confirm that top 3 search intents have at least one matching quickstart or SDK guide.
- Continuous: triage doc bugs surfaced from support@redwood.ai; critical regressions flagged to on-call.

How to propose a docs change
1. Open a PR in docs repo with change and link to related SDK PR if applicable.
2. Add reviewer tags: @devex-writer and @sdk-maintainer.
3. Run local smoke tests (scripts/docs-smoke.sh) and attach results.
4. If change touches an API contract or SDK behavior, include changelog entry and coordinate a release note with Product.

Appendix: Useful CLI snippets
- Run docs smoke tests locally:
  ./scripts/docs-smoke.sh --targets quickstarts,home
- Run link checker (CI uses linkinator):
  npx linkinator http://localhost:3000 --ignore "/internal-only"
